title: Impact of UCHL1 on cellular, clinical and therapeutic properties in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
summary: The aims of the planned study are: (i) a better understanding of UCHL1 regulation and function in carcinogenesis, genotoxic stress and the interaction of cancer cells with the immunological TME, and (ii) a solid and evidence-based foundation for new therapeutic concepts for tumours with a UCHL1-dependent phenotype. Based on our own preliminary work, we anticipate that the expected results will provide added scientific value for other cancers beyond HNSCC and, in the long term, enable the translation of innovative therapeutic concepts into future clinical trials.
conditions: Malignant neoplasms of lip, oral cavity and pharynx
Malignant neoplasm of nasal cavity and middle ear

interventions.name: Only cancer patients with a confirmed diagnosis of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) who have been treated at the Heidelberg University Hospital (experimental validation with tumour samples) or are currently undergoing treatment (experimental validation in the preclinical model) are elig

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Confirmed diagnosis of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
- Availability of tumour samples from the NCT tissue bank 
    (experimental validation with tumour tissue)
- Planned surgical tumour resection as part of routine treatment at the University Hospital Heidelberg (experimental validation in the preclinical model)
Exclusion criteria:
- Nonage
- Patients who lack full legal capacity and consent
- Diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma not confirmed by histopathology
- Small size or quality of available tumour tissue
- Withdrawal of consent for use of samples or data
